growth_story.headline: After a deep collapse in the 1990s, Tajikistan has grown every year since 1998, lately carried by money from migrant workers and a gold mining boom.
growth_story.arc: Tajikistan's income per person collapsed in the early 1990s: from 1990 to 1997 it shrank by 14.4 percent a year, falling from 1,313 to 370 constant US dollars between 1990 and 1996. Since 1998 it has grown every year, by 5.3 percent a year on average, with only short slowdowns in 2009 and 2020. Growth picked up from 4.5 percent a year in 2006-2015 to 5.2 percent in 2016-2025, and was above 6 percent in each year from 2023 to 2025. Income per person passed its 1988 level in 2024 and reached a new peak of 1,593 in 2025. The IMF and the World Bank tie the recent pace to the rebound after Covid-19, to very large remittances from Tajiks working abroad, and to fast growth in gold and other mining.

threads.title: Remittances from work abroad
threads.text: Money sent home by Tajiks working abroad is a main force behind recent growth. It has propped up household and other spending at home, and it has stayed well above its level before 2022 because demand for migrant workers has been strong.

citations.title: Tajikistan Economic Update 2025
citations.quote: Domestic demand was supported by large remittance inflows—peaking at 49% of GDP in 2024 compared to 39% in 2023—and higher public sector wages.

citations.title: Republic of Tajikistan: 2025 Article IV Consultation and Second Review under the Policy Coordination Instrument and Request for Modification of a Reform Target-Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for Republic of Tajikistan
citations.quote: Remittances in 2024 remained well above pre-2022 levels, in line with developments in the Central Asia region, reflecting strong demand for migrant labor

threads.title: A gold mining boom
threads.text: Gold output has risen fast, especially since a large new mine opened in 2022, and mining is mostly run as joint ventures with Chinese investors. Mining made up a visible part of growth in 2024.

citations.title: Republic of Tajikistan: 2025 Article IV Consultation and Second Review under the Policy Coordination Instrument and Request for Modification of a Reform Target-Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for Republic of Tajikistan
citations.quote: Annual production reached about 14.2 tons in 2024 following the opening of a new large mining operation in 2022.

citations.title: Republic of Tajikistan: 2025 Article IV Consultation and Second Review under the Policy Coordination Instrument and Request for Modification of a Reform Target-Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for Republic of Tajikistan
citations.quote: Gold mining is carried out primarily through joint ventures with investors from China

citations.title: Republic of Tajikistan: 2025 Article IV Consultation and Second Review under the Policy Coordination Instrument and Request for Modification of a Reform Target-Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for Republic of Tajikistan
citations.quote: The contribution of mining to overall GDP growth accounted for about 12 percent in 2024.

threads.title: The bounce back after Covid-19
threads.text: Growth of income per person slowed to 2.1 percent in 2020 and jumped to 7.0 percent in 2021. The IMF says growth has since run above what the economy can keep up, lifted by the rebound and a surge of money from abroad, and it expects growth to slow over the medium term.

citations.title: Republic of Tajikistan: 2025 Article IV Consultation and Second Review under the Policy Coordination Instrument and Request for Modification of a Reform Target-Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for Republic of Tajikistan
citations.quote: Growth has remained above potential during this period due to the strong economic rebound from the Covid-19 lows, the post-Covid surge in remittances

citations.title: Republic of Tajikistan: 2025 Article IV Consultation and Second Review under the Policy Coordination Instrument and Request for Modification of a Reform Target-Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for Republic of Tajikistan
citations.quote: Real GDP growth is expected to moderate to 4.5 percent over the medium-term

threads.title: Exposure to Russia
threads.text: Because so much income comes from work abroad, the World Bank lists Russia's rules on migrant labor among the risks to growth. In 2026 Russia's escalating war in Ukraine disrupted fuel imports into Tajikistan.

citations.title: Tajikistan Economic Update 2025
citations.quote: Economic outlook faces several downside risks that stem from Russia’s labor migration policies, global policy instability, and ongoing regional conflicts.

citations.title: Asian Development Outlook September 2026: Caucasus and Central and West Asia
citations.quote: The ADO reduces Tajikistan’s 2026 growth forecast as Russia’s war in Ukraine has escalated, disrupting fuel imports and constraining near-term activity.

threads.title: Few exports beyond gold
threads.text: Apart from gold, Tajikistan sells little abroad, and exports fell in 2024 when shipments of precious metals and cotton dropped.

citations.title: Republic of Tajikistan: 2025 Article IV Consultation and Second Review under the Policy Coordination Instrument and Request for Modification of a Reform Target-Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for Republic of Tajikistan
citations.quote: Non-gold exports averaged 11 percent of GDP during 2020-2024.

citations.title: Tajikistan Economic Update 2025
citations.quote: Higher consumption and investment compensated for a 20.5% drop in exports, mainly due to reduced shipments of precious metals and cotton.

since_last_year.text: Growth stayed strong into 2026. In September 2026 the Asian Development Bank reported fast growth in the first half of the year, led by manufacturing, food processing and metallurgy, but it lowered its forecast for the year as Russia's war in Ukraine escalated and disrupted fuel imports.

citations.title: Asian Development Outlook September 2026: Caucasus and Central and West Asia
citations.quote: Tajikistan’s growth remained strong at 8.2% in the first half, led by expansion in manufacturing, food processing, and metallurgy, and strong retail-driven services.

citations.title: Asian Development Outlook September 2026: Caucasus and Central and West Asia
citations.quote: The ADO reduces Tajikistan’s 2026 growth forecast as Russia’s war in Ukraine has escalated, disrupting fuel imports and constraining near-term activity.

growth_story.tension: The sources' headline growth rates are for the whole economy and are much higher than growth in income per person, which was 6.3 percent in 2024, because the population keeps growing. The sources also expected growth to slow in 2025 as remittances settled down, yet income per person grew a little faster in 2025, at 6.4 percent. None of the sources read here explains the collapse of 1990-1997; the story of that era rests on the data alone.
